first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and inherited evidence indicates shorter, simpler onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. Promotional pricing may address immediate competitive pressure but has a documented 30-day retention cost, conflicting with sustainable qualified revenue. Verify the original onboarding and pricing records before committing because only one slot is available.

mid.rationale: Run a simplified onboarding experiment for self-serve/SMB accounts. It directly addresses the 4% completion decline and the associated activation weakness, with confirmed prior results of +13% completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and +3% 30-day retention. This supports durable qualified revenue rather than discount-led acquisition; verified promotional pricing raised qualified revenue short term but reduced 30-day retention by 12%.

final2.rationale: Maintain the simplified-onboarding experiment. It addresses both current operational declines and has verified durable evidence: higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention. The deeper competitor cut raises urgency, but the available pricing evidence shows targeted discounting produces a 12% 30-day retention decline and is not a sustainable qualified-revenue response.
